summary: Laura Harrington works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. She studied at Columbia University under Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi Jr., Gary A. Tubb, Geshe Lobsang Jamspal, Kirti Rinpoche, Nathaniel Dickson, and Gregory Hillis.

Lauran R. Hartley is a Tibetologist who has served as a visiting assistant professor at Indiana University Bloomington, taught at Rutgers University (attested 2003), and served as an Adjunct Assistant Professor and Director of the Modern Tibetan Studies Program at Columbia University (attested 2026).

Laurence Austine Waddell (1854-1938) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a medical degree from the University of Glasgow (~1874-1878). He served in the Indian Medical Service and Indian Army, taught at Kolkata's Medical College, and was Professor of Tibetan at UCL (1906-1908).

Laurence Binyon (1869-1943) was a scholar in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. Educated at St Paul's School and Trinity College, Oxford, he worked at the British Museum (~1893-1933) and held a post at Harvard University (~1933-1934).

Laurie L. Patton (born 1961) works in Indology and religious studies, holding degrees from Harvard and the University of Chicago. She served as Professor and Dean at Duke, President of Middlebury College (2015-2024), and became President of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences (~2024).
Lavanya V. Eswar is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. As of 2026, she is attested as a Ph.D. scholar studying at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.

Lawrence E. Sullivan (born 1949) is a scholar of religious studies, history, and archaeology. He held posts as Director at Harvard University (attested 2000) and the Center for the Study of World Religions (attested 2004), and as Professor of Theology at Notre Dame (attested 2005).

Lawrence Heyworth Mills (1837-1918) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at New York University and held a professorship at the University of Oxford (attested 1903).
Lawrence J. McCrea is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied under Sheldon Pollock. He serves as a professor at Cornell University (attested 2026).

Lawrence William Nelson is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Doctor of Philosophy and Religion from the California Institute of Integral Studies, having also studied at Butler, Indiana, NYU, Northwestern, St. John's College, and other institutions.
Laxmidhar Behera is a scholar in computational fields and Indology. He has held academic posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur and the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi.

Le Manh That (born 1944) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a BA from the University of Saigon (~1962-1965), a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965-1974), and held a post at Van Hanh University (~1974-1975).
LeRoy Carr Barret (1877-1960) was an Indologist. He studied at Washington and Lee University (~1895-1898) and at Johns Hopkins University (~1899-1903) under Maurice Bloomfield.
Leah Zahler (1937-2000) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins, Harvey B. Aronson, and Geshe Wangyal.
Lee Yearley is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He held a professorship at Stanford University (attested 1989-1992), where he is currently attested as Emeritus (2026).

Leedom Lefferts specializes in Buddhist studies and anthropology. He has served as Professor of Anthropology, Emeritus, at Drew University (attested 2011) and as a Research Associate in the Department of Anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution (attested 2011).

Leela Aditi Wood is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan (completed by 2005) under Luis O. Gómez and Martin J. Powers, and held a post at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Leo M. Pruden (1937-1991) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taitetsu Unno and at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa. He held posts at Brown University (1970-1971), Nyingma Institute (1971), and University of Oriental Studies (attested 1988-1991).

Leo Meyer (1830-1910) was a linguist who studied at Göttingen and Berlin under Benfey, Grimm, and Bopp. He served as a professor at the University of Göttingen (1862-1865, chair in 1898) and held the chair of German and comparative linguistics at Tartu/Dorpat (1865-1899).
Leo Rishi Nelson Jones is an Indologist affiliated with the University of Hamburg, where he studied and holds a post as a Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter (attested 2026).
